name: Imagined Worlds: Fantasy and Science Fiction
description: From the Monkey King and Camelot to Oz, Middle-earth and Hogwarts: how fantasy and science fiction built worlds readers could live in.

checkpoints.name: Old marvels
checkpoints.note: Long before the word fantasy, storytellers in Britain and China told of a king with a round table and a monkey who fought Heaven.

checkpoints.name: Scientific romances
checkpoints.note: Shelley, Carroll, Verne and Wells imagined creatures made by science, a girl underground, submarines, time travel and invasion from Mars.

checkpoints.name: Invented lands
checkpoints.note: Baum's Oz and Tolkien's Middle-earth showed that an author could build a whole country, while Huxley and Orwell turned the future into a warning.

checkpoints.name: The fantasy boom
checkpoints.note: Narnia, The Lord of the Rings and Dune sold in the millions, and Star Trek and Star Wars brought science fiction to the screen. Fantasy and science fiction became big business.

checkpoints.name: Worlds without end
checkpoints.note: Blade Runner, cyberspace and The Matrix, a comic Discworld, wizards in Scotland and arenas of teenagers made fantasy and science fiction the main fiction of the age.
